HELD: Modvat: Inputs--Refractories used in the steel industry are not inputs as per Explanation under Rule 57A, and hence are not eligible for Modvat. ".. ...we hold that refractories used in the steel industry are hit by the explanation to Rule 57A, because of the fact that they go in relation to the machinery and form part of the machinery and equipment and therefore the authorities below are justified in disallowing the credit in respect of the duty paid on this item."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit - Inputs - Whether Notification No. 14/1997 dated 3-5-1997 restricting admissibility of Modvat credit for all petroleum products to extent of 10 per cent irrespective of fact as to whether inputs were manufactured in India or inputs were imported into India, being violative of article 14 of the Constitution of India, is to be quashed and set-aside - Held, yes [Para 40] [In favour of assessee] Circulars & Notifications : Notification Nos. 5/94-CE(NT), dated 1-3-1994, 14/97 CE (N.T.), dated 3-5-1997 and 60/97, dated 27-11-1997 Interpretation of Statutes : Maxim sublato fundamento cadit opus Words and Phrases : Expression paid on inputs as occurring in rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1994

FACT: Paraffin was a specified petroleum product under Central Excise Tariff Act, 1985. Said product was chargeable to excise duty at rate of 15 per cent ad valorem when manufactured or produced in India. However under APM regime public sector refineries were directed to recover 10 per cent from customers and short-fall of 5 per cent was reimbursed to them from oil pool account. When said product is imported it is chargeable to customs duty including an additional customs duty of 15 per cent ad valorem. The assessee was importer of said product. In view of Notification No. 5/94-CE (N.T.), dated 1-3-1994 duty paid on paraffin was eligible for Modvat credit to the extent of payment of specified duty, i.e., 15 per cent. However, Government noticed that there were unscrupulous practice apparently adopted by certain entities paying only 10 per cent excise duty to refineries in respect of APM products and obtaining 15 per cent Modvat credit on ground of 'duty paid on inputs'. Therefore, impugned Notification No. 14/97-CE (N.T.), dated 3-5-1997 was issued to amend Notification No. 5/94-CE (N.T.), dated 1-3-1994, restricting admissibility of Modvat credit at rate of 10 per cent ad valorem on paraffin, irrespective of fact whether same were imported or manufactured or produced in India. Said notification was given retrospective effect from 23-7-1996. As a result of this, the credit taken in excess of 10 per cent ad valorem was required to be paid by manufacturers. When the Government realized by November, 1997 that the case of direct imports of inputs in the nature of petroleum products were erroneously covered under the impugned Notification because the duty at the rate of 15 per cent was paid on such imported inputs by the concerned importers like the assessee, the Government rectified this error only prospectively, i.e., from 27-11-1997. As the assessee failed to pay back the credit taken, show-cause notice was issued to it demanding duty. On adjudication, the demand was confirmed which was upheld by the Commissioner (Appeals). The petitioner without challenging order-in-appeal before Tribunal filed instant writ petition on ground that impugned notification was unconstitutional and ultra vires.

HELD: The assessee-company imported a consignment of paraffin wax on payment of customs duty including additional customs duty (also known as 'counter vailing duty' or 'CVD'), and such inputs were used in relation to manufacture of the finished products namely paraffin wax. There is no dispute to the fact that CVD was actually paid by the assessee at the rate of 15 per cent ad valorem because Central excise duty leviable on, such petroleum products manufactured in India was 15 per cent ad valorem and CVD/additional customs duty is levied and collected on goods imported in India at the rate of excise duty applicable to like goods produced or manufactured in India. Thus, all the consignments of paraffin were imported by the assessee has actually suffered incidence of additional customs duty at the rate of 15 per cent ad valorem. [Para 9]

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Burden of proof--There is no general rule that burden lies on department--manufacturer's stand regarding inputs contested by department--Tribunal to interpret notifications and decide relying on its own decisions

FACT: These are appeals filed against orders of Collector of Central Excise, on grounds that the burden does not lie on the department to prove that certain input is recognisable as being non-duty paid or charged to nil rate of duty.

HELD: Modvat Credit--As the manufacturer had taken a stand regarding the inputs and the department had contested the claim, Tribunal had to interpret, and apply notification. Being a covered matter the orders in reference, passed by the Tribunal apply to the present case. "In the cases before us, the manufacturers have taken a definite Stand with regard to the inputs in question and the department has contested the claim. Therefore, the Tribunal was required to interpret and apply notifications and announce the orders........As far as we can see the department has not been able to show how the Punjab and Haryana High Court judgment could help their cause in these circumstances..........We see no reason to differ from the orders already passed and cited above which admittedly apply to the present cases......Accordingly the appeals are rejected."

chargeable to Nil rate of duty. Rule 57CC was introduced in 1996 for adjustment of credit in inputs used in exempted final products or maintenance of separate inventory and accounts of inputs by the manufacturer. Rule 57CC of the Rules, 1944 is corresponding to rule 57AD(2) of Rules 1944 and rule 6(2) of the Rules, 2001, Rules 2002 and Rules, 2004. [Para 18] The Rajasthan High Court in the case of Hindustan Zinc Ltd. v. Union of India 2008 (223) ELT 149 while dealing with rule 57C and rule 57CC relying on the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of Dai Ichi Karkaria Ltd. (supra) and the Kerala High Court’s decision in the case of CCE v. Premier Tyres Ltd. 2001 (130) ELT 451 held that if on the date of entitlement, there is no illegality or invalidity in taking credit of such Modvat/Cenvat credit, right to utilization of such credit against further liability towards duty become indefeasible and is not liable to be recovered in such contingency. [Para 19]

On a perusal of rule 6 and the corresponding rules, as mentioned above, it was clear that the assessee had correctly taken the credit and utilized it, when the final product was dutiable and there was no requirement to reverse the credit on final product becoming exempt and such credit could not be recovered under rule 12 corresponding to rules 57-I and 57AH. [Para 20]

In view of the above discussion, it was to be held that when the input credit was legally taken and utilized on the dutiable final products it need not be reversed on the final product becoming exempt subsequently with effect from 9-7-2004. The decision of the Bangalore Bench in the case of TAFE Ltd. (Tractor Division) (supra) enunciated the correct position of the law. The issue was, thus, answered in favour of the assessee and against the revenue. [Para 22]

CASE REVIEWED

TAFE Ltd. (Tractor Division) v. CCE 2007 (79) RLT 706 (Tri. - Bang.) approval (para 22)

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Aluminium sheets, being essentially required for production of unwrought zinc are eligible for Modvat

HELD: Modvat credit--Aluminium sheets essentially required for the manufacture of unwrought zinc are eligible for Modvat credit being an input used in relation to the manufacture of the said products."........Aluminium sheets are an essential requirement in the electrolysis process and these have to be replaced from time to time after they lose their utility and the waste is sold as scrap. Use of Aluminium sheets is directly in the manufacturing process and since these cannot be treated as equipment by itself, use of the same has to be taken to be in relation to the manufacture of the specified final product under Rule 57A........we hold that the appellants are eligible for the benefit of MODVAT credit......."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat Credit - Modvat - EOUs--Credit not admissible for goods cleared to EOUs free of duty

FACT: Appellants manufacture Pumpable Slurry Explosives (PSE) and supply the same free of duty to a 100% Export Oriented Unit (EOU). The appellants want to be allowed to accumulate Modvat credit on inputs of PSE for utilisation later as and when they start clearing the goods on payment of duty.

HELD: Modvat--credit is not admissible as no duty leviable on the final product (PSE) cleared by the appellants. "A reading of the various Central Excise Rules and the Scheme of the MODVAT set out therein shows that the facility of MODVAT Credit is available in respect of duty paid on inputs used in or in relation to the manufacture of the specified final product and for utilizing the credit so allowed towards payment of duty of excise leviable on the final product. When, therefore, there is no duty leviable on the final products which have been cleared from the appellants' factory, the question of allowing them the MODVAT Credit on the inputs would not arise. Rule 57C of the Central Excise Rules clearly envisages that no credit of the specified duty paid on the inputs used in the manufacture of a final product shall be allowed if the final product is exempt from the whole of the duty of excise leviable thereon or is chargeable to nit rate of duty. ...In view of above, we hold that there is no force in the appellants' plea......."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat credit - Modvat - Hydrochloric/Sulphuric Acid, Hydrazine and Sodium Sulphate used in paper manufacture for demineralisation of water or as dc-oxidants are entitled to Modvat benefit

FACT: In the process of manufacturing paper, hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid are used for demineralisation of water which is then turned into steam which is used for the drying of paper. Hydrazine 100% and Sodium Sulphate are used as deoxidants to carry oxygen in the water treatment plants. The issue that arises for determination is whether the items mentioned above can be considered as inputs used in relation to the manufacture of paper, thus being entitled to MODVAT Credit.

HELD: MODVAT--Hydrochloric acid, sulphuric acid, hydrozine 100% and sodium sulphate used in the manufacture of paper are eligible for MODVAT credit as subject inputs have a nexus with a process which is integrally connected with the ultimate production of paper (ratio of earlier decision in Andhra Pradesh Paper Mills Ltd. v. CCE). ".......following the ratio of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and of this Tribunal........we hold that both Hydrochloric and Sulphuric Acid would be eligible for the benefit of MODVAT Credit, as these are used for treatment of water as seen from the order of the lower appellate authority. So far as Hydrazene 100% is concerned, it is also used for treatment of water. Its use is for the generation of steam which is used in the manufacturing process and we hold that Hydrazene 100% is also eligible for the benefit of MODVAT Credit. In view of above, we find no merits in the appeal of the Revenue and therefore we reject the same."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat Credit - Modvat - Inputs for cement--goods required directly or in relation to the manufacture of goods are eligible. Items to be used as consumer goods such as those for mining limestone are not inputs for cement

FACT: Modvat credit in respect of certain inputs claimed by the appellants to be used as inputs in or in relation to the manufacture of cement was rejected by the Department and upheld by the Collector (Appeals).

HELD: Modvat--Inputs used in the manufacture of cement--Under Rule 57A of Central Excise Rules, credit is admissible only on such inputs as are used directly in or in relation to the manufacture of the final product. Therefore, items required for mining of limestone, maintenance of structures, mining machinery, transport, etc. are not eligible inputs (ratio of earlier judgment), "...we find that the use of the different goods listed by the appellants is for quarrying of limestone, plant repair, industrial structures, maintenance, kiln lining, transportation, roofing of factory structures, hand gloves and shoes for safety. Laboratory glassware for laboratory use...locomotive spares etc. ...What can be permitted for Modvat benefit under Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules are goods used in or in relation to manufacture subject to exclusions like machinery etc. Goods required for maintenance of structures, equipment and machinery are not eligible inputs. They are used in relation to maintenance and repair of the machinery, equipment and not used in relation to the manufacture of the final products. Goods used for mining of limestone or maintenance of mining machinery or equipment or for transport are likewise ineligible for the benefit of Modvat credit. The order in appeal does not disclose any infirmity in regard to the denial of Modvat credit on such goods"

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Act, 1944 - Modvat credit - Inputs - Appellant-job-worker manufactured plastic half round rain water system out of raw material supplied by manufacturer-supplier - Benefit of notification 1/93 was denied to appellant because as per appellants goods were classifiable under head 32.26.90 and according to department goods were fall under head 39.17.00 - On appeal Tribunal denied said benefit and remitted back matter for revaluation of duty by classifying manufactured goods under head 39.17.00 and directed for allowing Modvat credit accordingly - However, on readjudication, Modvat credit was denied - Whether since supply of goods by manufacturer to job-worker was well established, Modvat credit would have to be granted - Held, yes [Matter remanded for redetermine value] Circulars & Notifications: Notification No. 1/93

FACT: The appellant-job-workers manufactured ‘Plastic half round rain water system’ using raw material supplied by the manufacturer. The appellants claimed benefit of notification No. 1 of 1993 which was denied because the goods manufactured were bearing brand name of manufacturer. Classification of goods manufactured as well as turnover limitation and valuation of goods were in dispute. The Tribunal held that goods manufactured were classifiable either under heading 39.25.99 or under heading 39.17.00 and remitted the matter back to redetermine the valuation and eligibility of Modvat after denying benefit of Notification as well as plea of limitation. On readjudication the Modvat credit was denied. The Commissioner determined demand and imposed penalty.

On appeal :

HELD: The limitation issue was settled by the earlier order of the Tribunal and it was not open to reopen that issue. However, the question of classification in the instant case was annexed issue. The imposition of penalty, therefore, was not called for. There was no cause for imposition of penalty in these appeals. More so when, section 11AC penalty for certain period, in this case could not be invoked, being period earlier to introduction of that section. As regards the plea made on interest under section 11AB, the application of Board Instruction No. 655/46/2002-CX, dated 26-6-2002 would govern and be applicable in this case to levy interest. The valuation was to be redetermined as per the formula prescribed by the Apex Court in the case of Ujjagar Print. The CA certificate had to be considered to determine the valuation and duty. As regards the plea of Modvat, there was no valid reasons to deny the same as arrived at in the order impugned. Since goods have been supplied by manufacturer to the job-workers, the Modvat credit would have to be granted and thereafter duty demand was to be reverted. [Para 4]

In view of the finding, these appeals were partly allowed after setting aside the penalty as imposed and the matter was remitted back to the Commissioner to re-determine the valuation of goods and quantum of duty and interest. [Para 5]

HEADNOTE: Rule 57H of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Credit on inputs in stock on 1.3.1986 has to be allowed where proforma credit was admissible. Limitation inapplicable on such stocks

HELD: Modvat--Time limit under Rule 57H(2)--Benefit of Modvat credit available on zinc ingots lying in stock on 1.3.1986, and which had suffered duty prior to 31.1.1986, as credit was allowable in respect of such inputs under Rule 56A, prior to 1.3.1986. Time limit under Rule 57H(2) not applicable. "We observe that all that the Rule talks about is that the time bar regarding the payment of duty on or before 31.1.1986 for the purpose of availment of the Modvat credit would not be applicable where the inputs in respect of which credit was allowable under any Rule or Notification prior to 1st March, 1986. Once it is ascertained that this credit was allowable irrespective of the fact whether the appellants' actually availed of the credit or not, the appellants' case would fall within the exception of Rule 57H(2). We observe that this aspect had not been examined in the impugned order. Notwithstanding that, since it has been established and it is not contradicted by Revenue that the appellants' products fall within the ambit of Rule 56A, we hold that the benefit as pleaded in terms of Rule 57H(2) would be available to the appellants. The appellants as it is have been allowed the benefit in respect of the inputs which were lying in stock as on 1.3.1986 and which were received till 31.3.1986 and the appellants' claim was turned down only in cases where duty had been paid before 31.1.1986. Since we have held that this cut off date will not vitiate the appellants' claim, we allow the appeal."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Mercury used as cathode in the electrolytical process gets consumed and cannot be treated as equipment in relation co. manufacture of specified product--Eligible for Modvat credit under

FACT: M/s. Chemicals Mettur and Industrials claimed Modvat credit of duty on mercury, used as cathode in electrolytical process for manufacturing caustic soda. The Collector of Central Excise, Coimbatore disallowed credit being expenditure on purchase of mercury shown under the heading 'Capital Expenditure' and treating it part of capital equipment which is not eligible for Modvat credit. Collector of Central Excise (Appeals) allowed Modvat Credit.

HELD: Modvat Credit--Mercury used as cathode in the electrolytical process gets consumed and after use for some time, these are discarded as waste material. It cannot be treated as equipment in relation to manufacture of specified final product under CE Rule 57A. Ratio of case Cominco Binani Zinc Ltd. [1990 (28) ECR 421]. "...Aluminium sheets are an essential requirement in the electrolysis process and these have to be replaced from time to time after they lose their utility and waste is sold as scrap. Use of Aluminium sheets is directly in the manufacturing process and since these cannot be treated as equipment by itself, use of the same has to be taken to be in relation to the manufacture of the specified final product under Rule 57A as in the case of the Titanium Metal Anodes in respect of which Modvat credit has been held to be admissible. It is observed that the term inputs' used under Rule 57A. has a wider import. Aluminium sheets used being no equipment as such and since these participate in the manufacturing process, have to be taken to be covered by the provisions of Rule 57A for grant of Modvat credit".

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat (Modvat) - Conditions for allowing of - Argon Gas - Eligible for Modvat being used in manufacture of tool tips. Freon T-DA 35X also eligible

HELD: Modvat--Argon Gas and Freon T-DA 35X eligible for Modvat being used in or in relation to the manufacture of tool tips and tools--Argon gas for providing the inert atmosphere and T-DA 35X as a drying agent. "It is seen from the write up given and the literature produced that both Argon gas and Freon T-DA 35-X are used in the manufacturing stream of the goods viz. tool tips and tools manufactured by the appellant. The use of Argon gas for providing the inert atmosphere for the necessary processing on the carbide components is a technical necessity and obviously without providing the inert atmosphere the work pieces would not acquire the necessary properties as pleaded by me appellant. In view of this we hold that the benefit of Modvat credit in respect of Argon gas has to be allowed.......In regard to the use of Freon T-DA 35-X, it is clearly set out in the literature that it is used as a drying agent and for taking away the moisture from the surfaces of the work pieces before the same can be put in the market stream. We observe the appellant is manufacturing high quality tools and any moisture on these may ultimately result in some damage to the pieces. Inasmuch as the drying has to be done before the finished product is put in the market stream the use of the item in question, therefore, has to be taken to be in or in relation to the manufacture of the finished product. In view of the above we hold that the appellant's plea has to be allowed with consequential relief. The appeal is, therefore, allowed."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Modvat - Deemed credit - Scrap captively produced in a factory for subsequent manufacture of ERW and SW pipes from duty-paid H.R. Coil, is not eligible - As nil duty was paid on the inputs, they are not duty-paid goods - Notfn. 54/86-CE

FACT: Modvat credit was disallowed for scrap arising in the appellants' steel plant in the course of manufacture of E.R.W. and SW pipes from duty-paid H.R. Coil. The scrap is useful only for melting. The Collector (Appeals) upheld the Assistant Collector's order that deemed credit cannot be granted because the scrap was exempt from duty and the facility was available only for inputs clearly recognisable as being non-duty-paid or chargeable to nil rate of duty.

HELD: Modvat--deemed credit not available for scrap captively produced in a factory for subsequent manufacture of E.R.W. and SW pipes from duty-paid H.R. Coil. The deemed credit facility is not available for scrap which was exempt from duty as non-duty-paid goods. Clearing the goods without payment of duty amounts to clearing them on payment of appropriate duty leviable i.e. nil rate of duty. Since nil duty has been paid on the inputs, only nil duty will qualify for Modvat credit. "The argument that goods are exempted from the whole of duty leviable thereon and hence clearing the goods without payment of duty actually amounts to clearing them in payment of the appropriate duty leviable thereon namely nil duty docs not make them duty-paid goods for the purpose of granting Modvat credit. Modvat credit facility is for utilising the duty-paid in the inputs for payment of duty payable on the outputs arising therefrom. If nil duty has been paid on the inputs, by virtue of the exemption notification, then it is that nil duty that will qualify for Modvat credit.........the goods captively produced in a factory for subsequent manufacture therein are specifically outside the scope of the deemed credit orders contemplated under the second proviso to Rule-57G(2)........"

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat credit - Modvat - Caustic soda lye inputs used in manufacture of PVC resins entitled to credit

FACT: The Revenue have filed this appeal being aggrieved by the Collector's order holding that the inputs used for the manufacture of caustic soda lye and caustic soda flakes which are finally used in the manufacture of PVC resins and are covered by the exemption notification, are eligible for Modvat credit.

HELD: Modvat credit--Inputs used in the manufacture of intermediate products which are ultimately used in the manufacture of the final product are eligible for the benefit of Modvat scheme. "So long as it can be shown that the inputs have been used for manufacture of any in processed materials which are used in the manufacture of final product, the said material manufactured out of the inputs before it is finally used in the manufacture of the declared final product will have to be treated as intermediate product. There is nothing on record to show nor is there any plea that caustic soda lye and caustic soda flakes which emerged during the manufacturing process by use of the inputs were not used as in process material for the manufacture of declared final product. In view of above, we hold that the lower appellate authority's order is maintainable in law. We, therefore dismiss the appeal of the Revenue."

The appeal of the manufacturer was, accordingly, allowed and it was held that the MODVAT credit was allowable on the use of the explosives in the manufacture of cement irrespective of the fact that the explosives were used directly in the mines and never entered the factory of the manufacturer of cement. [Para 8] In 2000, the MODVAT Rules were replaced by the CENVAT Rules by the Central Excise (Second Amendment) Rules, 2000. Basically there was a re-arrangement of the earlier rules which in substance remained the same.

It is clear that sub-rule (d ) of rule 57AA (as introduced in 2000) had merely reframed rule 57B to include all the ingredients of inputs while at the same time broadening the base not only by referring to ‘all goods’ but also by using the word ‘includes’. [Para 9]

Rule 57AC provides for the conditions for allowing CENVAT credit in respect of inputs received in the factory of the manufacturer. [Para 10]

Initially, rule 57J of the MODVAT Rules was deleted. Consequently, with the intention of re-introducing the benefit granted earlier under rule 57J, rule 57AB was introduced under the heading ‘CENVAT credit’. [Para 11]

Rule 57AB effectively duplicates the substance of rule 57J(1) and (2) and deals with a situation where inputs are received by a job worker for production of intermediate goods which are used in the manufacture of a final product. [Para 12]

In J.K. Udyog Ltd.’s case (supra), three reasons were given by the Supreme Court for holding that credit could be taken only on inputs received in the factory of the manufacturer of the final product. First, the Court held that the definition of input given in sub-rule(d) of rule 57AA was entirely different from the manner in which the said word had been expounded in the Explanation to rule 57A of the MODVAT Rules. However, there was only a re-arrangement of the several provisions of rule 57B in rule 57AA. Rule 57AA is in fact more broad based than rule 57B.

Second, the Court proceeded on the basis that under the CENVAT scheme, there was no provision similar to rule 57J of the MODVAT scheme. However, rule 57J was replaced in substance by rule 57AB. That provision was overlooked.

Another reason given by the Court in J.K. Udaipur Udyog case (supra ) for holding that the CENVAT scheme was different from the MODVAT Scheme was rule 57AC(1). However, that rule was limited to inputs received in the factory of the manufacturer and did not impinge on rule 57AB at all.

The schemes of MODVAT and CENVAT Credit are not, therefore, different and the conclusion of the Court in J.K. Udaipur Udyog that the decision in Jaypee Rewa Cement (supra ) would have no application to CENVAT Rules could not be accepted. [Para 14]

The CENVAT Rules in effect substitute the MODVAT Rules and the decision in Jaypee Rewa Cement would continue to apply. The decision in CCE v. J.K. Udaipur Udyog Ltd. (supra ) holding to the contrary, was not good law. [Para 15]

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit - Conditions of allowing of

HELD: Modvat - Control panels and circuit breakers, procured from others, are component parts of diesel generators. Credit admissible [ratio of Supreme Court decisions in Eastend Paper Industries 1990 (26) ECR 10 (SC) and J.K. Cotton Spg. & Wvg. Mills Co. Ltd.] CE Rule 57A. "The ratio of the Supreme Court decisions would clearly establish the appellants' case for granting of Modvat benefit in respect of the specified duty paid on the inputs, Control Panel and Air Circuit Breaker used in or in relation to the manufacture of the final product, diesel generating sets......Not only is the inclusion of the value of the inputs in question in the assessable value of the final product the material factor but the fact that these inputs are actually fitted in the generating sets and perform specific functions therein to make it properly functional will remove any doubt in this regard"

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat Credit - Modvat - Input (lead, zinc) need not be present in the product (MS steel). If used in or in relation to, credit admissible. Notfn. 177/86-CE

FACT: The appellants manufacture MS steel products in which lead, along with zinc was used in the process of galvanisation. Both the inputs and the final products have been notified in Notification No. 177/86-CE and are entitled to Modvat credit. The Assistant Collector denied them Modvat credit on the ground that lead was neither consumed in the process of manufacture of final product, nor can it be termed as input. Hence the appeal against the order of CCE (Appeals).

HELD: Modvat--Rule 57A--Explanation--Modvat credit allowed as long as inputs are used in or in relation to the manufacture of final products and are not specifically excluded from the scope of the benefit in the explanation clause in Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 or by exclusion in Notification No. 177/86-CE. "There is no requirement that inputs should be present in the final product or it should be consumed in order to qualify for modvat benefit. It is clear that to become input it must be used in or in relation to the manufacture of goods. If lead is used in the process of manufacture of final product, there cannot be any doubt in availing modvat credit as per Explanation to Rule 57-A. As long as they are used in or in relation to the manufacture of the final products and are not specifically excluded from the scope of the benefit......in the explanation clause in Rule 57-A of the Central Excise Rules or by exclusion in Notification No. 177/86-CE, dated 1st March, 1986, modvat credit has to be allowed."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat credit - Modvat - Cement--Packaging--Paper bags for cement not eligible as cement also sold in bulk

HELD: Modvat--Input--Paper bags used as packing material is not an Input in or in relation to the manufacture of cement As cement is also admittedly sold in bulk, paper bags are not a pre-requisite for fulling the cement in the market stream. "Even if a very broad and charitable view is taken with reference to the scope of Rule 57A, it would be difficult to hold that paper bags used as packing material is an input in the manufacture or in relation to the manufacture of cement. To a specific query the learned counsel in all fairness submitted that cement is also sold in bulk. Therefore, in the context of the Scheme of MODVAT and having regard to the process of manufacture of cement and its distribution, it is not a pre-requisite for putting the cement in the market stream. In this view of the matter, we uphold the order of the lower appellate authority."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Modvat credit is admissible on anodes (coated titanium) falling under H. 8108.00 as these are used in or in relation to manufacture of caustic soda. 'Input' the term used under Rule 57A has a wider import. Wider meaning is to be given to the expression 'used in or in relation to the manufacture' of goods in the context of Rule 57A

HELD: Modvat Credit--the expression 'used in or in relation to the manufacture' of goods in the context of Rule 57A has a wider amplitude. Coated Titanium anodes falling under Tariff sub-heading 8108.00 and utilised in the manufacture of caustic soda in the electrolysis process are eligible for Modvat credit (ratio of earlier judgments). "It is observed that the wider meaning is desired to be given to the expression 'used in or in relation to the manufacture' of goods in the context of Rule 57A and in that view of the matter, as held in the decision cited above, we find no reason to depart from the earlier decisions of the Tribunal. .....We observe that in view of the decision of this Bench in the case of Aluminium Sheets and that of the West Regional Bench in the case of Titanium Metal Anodes and also the decision of the Special Bench of the Tribunal in the context of Notification 201/79, the appellants' appeal will have to be allowed"

HEADNOTE: Section 57A read with section 2(f) of the Central Excise Act, 1944 - Modvat - Oil (Rust Preventive) eligible but not oxygen required for testing steel. Testing is not a process relating to manufacture

FACT: The Collector (Appeals) allowed Modvat credit to the respondents in respect of the inputs viz. rust preventive oil and oxygen allegedly used in relation to manufacture of Textile Machinery. Hence this appeal by the Revenue.

HELD: Following the ratio of earlier ruling of this Bench Modvat credit in respect of Rust Preventive Oil is confirmed. "The learned DR fairly conceded that the issue in respect of Rust Preventive Oil is already covered by the ruling of this Bench in favour of the respondent by Order No. 147/1990 dated 31.1.1990.........Following the ratio, of the ruling of this Bench cited supra, we confirm the order of the lower appellate authority allowing MODVAT credit in respect of Rust Preventive Oil......"

2. Oxygen used for testing steel cannot be considered an input in relation to the manufacture of the end product. Testing of steel is not an activity related to manufacture of end product. ".......it would be far fetched to contend that Oxygen is used as an input in relation to the manufacture of the end-product for the purpose of grant of MODVAT credit.........We have held in a number of decisions that where the materials are prepared by use of some inputs for final use in the process of manufacture the same would be eligible for the benefit of MODVAT credit. Testing could not be considered such an activity."

3. Order of the lower authority in regard to oxygen not proper and is set aside. "..........the learned lower authority's order in regard to Oxygen cannot be held to be proper one and, therefore, we set aside the impugned order so far as the MODVAT credit allowed in the case of Oxygen is concerned."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57F of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Waste arising in the manufacture of final product is not liable to duty unless specified in Tariff itself

FACT: The point for decision in this case is whether, in terms of Rule 57F(4)(a), the appellant has to pay duty on the waste resulting from the manufacture of polyethylene film manufactured out of duty-paid raw materials.

HELD: Modvat--Waste--Plastic waste arising in the course of manufacture of polyethylene film out of duty-paid raw material is not liable to duty. Provision of Rule 57F(4)(a) is not applicable to such waste (ratio of Tribunal Order No. 110/91-C dt. 21.1.1991 in Anand Polyrotex v. CCE, Bombay). "The Revenue had relied on the provisions of Central Excise Rule 57F(4)(a) to charge duty on the waste arising during the manufacture of polyethylene film out of duty-paid raw materials. In the aforesaid order the Tribunal held that the said rule by itself was not an authority for charging duty but permitted charging of duty if the waste was otherwise dutiable according to the Tariff and any relevant exemption notification. It was held that waste of plastic arising in the course of manufacture of polyethylene film out of duty-paid raw materials, covered by Chapter 39 of the Tariff Schedule, would not be chargeable to duty. .........Having considered the submissions, we see no reason to deviate from the previous decision. Accordingly, the impugned order is set aside and the appeal allowed."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat Credit - Modvat - Rubber chemicals/synthetic rubber insulate wires and cables - So these are intermediates - Modvat available - CE Notfn. 217/86-CE

HELD: Rubber chemicals and synthetic rubber form part of the compound providing insulation to wires and cables. It has to be construed as an intermediate product. Benefit of Modvat credit of duty paid on rubber chemicals and synthetic rubber thus available for payment of duty on Electric Wires and Cables."...........input for input of the final product is also an input for the final product. Hence, there is no misdeclaration in the modvat declaration.........rubber chemicals and synthetic rubber form part of the compound providing insulation to the electric wires and cables. They are components in a sense, physically present in the final product namely insulated wires and cables. All the components of a final product cannot be produced in a single stream. There could be more than one stream for different components. Rubber compound, being a component, gets manufactured separately and used in the manufacture of wires and cables. Hence, viewed in this background, it has to be construed as an intermediate product. In view of this, the benefit of Rule 57D is available to them. Credit of duty paid on synthetic rubber and other chemicals would be available for payment of duty on insulated wires and cables, notwithstanding the fact that rubber compound, which is a component, occurring at the intermediate stage, is exempted."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Credit earned can be utilised for payment of duty on products made out of non-duty-paid inputs also

FACT: The appellants manufacture steel ingots using as inputs various types of iron and steel scrap and ferro alloys. Some of these inputs are duty-paid on which Modvat credit was taken, while others are either chargeable at nil rate under some notification or at Nil additional/countervailing duty. A show cause notice was issued to the appellants alleging that they used the credit available on duty-paid inputs for paying duty on goods made out of inputs exempted from duty or chargeable at nil rate of duty. Demand was raised and penalty imposed on them on this account.

HELD: Modvat--The Trade Notice dated 8.8.1988 does not debar utilisation of Modvat credit taken on duty-paid inputs for payment of duty on similar goods manufactured out of non-duty-paid inputs. "The trade notice clarifies that Rule 57F(3) does not debar utilisation of excess for payment of duty on the same final products which are manufactured by non-duty paid inputs whether procured under Chapter X Procedure or otherwise exempt under any other Notification and also that there is no one to one co-relation of inputs and final product under the Modvat Scheme for utilisation of credit...........Modvat credit in terms of Rule 57F(3) availed of in lieu of excise duty already paid on inputs is available to the final products i.e. steel ingots admittedly manufactured out of duty paid inputs as well as from steel melting scrap and imported scrap............A plea was taken.........that the appellant was not manufacturing the steel ingots exclusively out of imported scrap but front combination with other scrap available in the stock. This plea was repeated.........that every batch of steel ingots manufactured by the appellants contained duty paid inputs on which MODVAT Credit was taken and no batch of steel ingots was made exclusively out of non-duty paid scrap in terms of notification 55/86 or imported scrap. This being the position every batch of steel ingots has utilised the inputs on which MODVAT Credit has been taken and therefore, duty payable on each such ingot can be paid out of the MODVAT Credit taken on inputs utilised in the steel ingots either wholly or partly as a manufacturer may desire. This is actually what has been done by the appellant herein. There is no contravention of Rule 57F(3), as alleged."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57AA of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat credit - Inputs - Whether CENVAT scheme brought in year 2000 is only a substitute of earlier Modvat scheme - Held, yes - Supreme Court in Jaypee Rewa Cement v. CCE 2001 (133) ELT 3 (SC) held that under MODVAT scheme for availing credit on inputs, inputs need not be utilized within factory premises - Whether said decision would equally apply to CENVAT Scheme and decision in CCE v. J.K. Udaipur Udyog Ltd. 2004 (171) ELT 289(SC) taking a contrary view, is not good law - Held, yes

FACT: The appellant was owner of a limestone mine which was situated at some distance from factory premises. Explosives and other inputs were used in quarrying limestone in the mine. Limestone was, in turn, used for manufacture of cement and clinkers in the factory. The revenue denied the CENVAT Credit availed by the appellant on explosives, etc.

The Supreme Court in a similar case of Jaypee Rewa Cement v. CCE 2001 (133) ELT 3 held that MODVAT credit would be allowable on the use of explosives in the manufacture of cement irrespective of the fact that explosives were directly used in mines and never entered the factory manufacturing cement. However, in the case of CCE v. J.K. Udaipur Udyog Ltd. 2004 (171) ELT 289 (SC), it was observed that schemes of MODVAT and CENVAT are different and, therefore, the decision of Jaypee Rewa Cement (supra) would have no application to the CENVAT Rules and credit would be allowable only on the inputs which are received in factory of manufacture of final product.

In the instant reference, the broader question arose for consideration as to whether there was a difference in substance between the MODVAT and the CENVAT schemes.

HELD: It is to be observed that rule 57B commences with a non obstante clause. It allows credit to be taken by a manufacturer of inputs used in or in relation to the manufacture of the final products whether directly or indirectly and whether contained in the final products or not. In the main body of sub-rule (1) there is no qualification as to where the inputs must be used. Qualifications have been introduced to the extent stated in clauses (i) to (vi), read with the Explanation. Clause (i) provides for inputs which are manufactured and used within the factory of production. Paints, fuel, packing materials and accessories are also treated as inputs without any requirement for user within the factory. Clause (iv) provides for credit on inputs used for generation of electricity or steam used for manufacture of the final products or for any other purposes ‘within the factory of production’. As far as the Explanation is concerned, the inputs are restricted to inputs notified under rule 57A.

There is no dispute that both explosives and limestone are notified under section 57A for manufacture of the final product viz., cement. [Para 4]

Under rule 57F, credit on inputs sent by a manufacturer from the factory to a job worker for test, repair, etc., but ultimately utilized in the final product is allowable. [Para 5]

Rule 57J allows credit on inputs used in manufacture of intermediate products described in column 3 of the Table provided the intermediate products are received by the manufacturer for use in or in relation to the manufacture of final products described in the corresponding Entry in column 4 of the Table. Explosives, limestone and cement are admittedly covered by column 1, 2 and 3 respectively of the Table. [Para 6]

In the case of Jaypee Rewa Cement (supra), the Supreme Court concluded that rule 57A(1) did not in any way specify that the inputs have to be utilized within the factory premises. It was further held that a reading of rule 57J and relevant notification can leave no manner of doubt that even in respect of inputs used in the manufacture of intermediate product which product is then used for the manufacture of a final product, the manufacturer would be allowed credit on the duty paid in respect of the input. On the explosives, duty had been paid and the appellants would be entitled to claim credit because the explosives were used for the manufacture of the intermediate product, namely, limestone which, in turn, was used for the manufacture of cement. The appeal of the manufacturer was, accordingly, allowed and it was held that the MODVAT credit was allowable on the use of the explosives in the manufacture of cement irrespective of the fact that the explosives were used directly in the mines and never entered the factory of the manufacturer of cement. [Para 8]

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Modvat - Co-relation of input to final product not necessary so long as utilisation is proved. CE Rule 57A allows credit; CE Rule 57F allows utilisation. The two cover separate stages. Reversal of credit not justified

FACT: The respondents are manufacturers of tyres. After filing a declaration under Rule 57G, they took Modvat credit for inputs specified in Rule 57A. Part of the finished goods were cleared free of duty under a notification. The issue for consideration is whether credit on the inputs going into that portion of the finished product, which is cleared free of duty under exemption notification has to be reversed.

HELD: No one-to-one co-relation has been prescribed between the inputs and finished product for the purpose of utilisation of Modvat credit All that is required is that credit should be utilized for discharging the duty liability on finished product. "It has to be observed that no one-to-one correlation has been prescribed between the inputs and the finished product for the purpose of utilisation of the MODVAT credit and all that is required is that the credit should be utilised for discharging the duty liability on the finished product which has been declared under Rule 57G(1) in respect of the inputs for which the MODVAT credit was taken."

2. The event of taking credit is provided for under Rule 57A and event of utilization of credit is provided for separately under Rule 57F. Each event has to be dealt with separately. "The Rules as are worded clearly provide for the utilisation of the credit taken in respect of the inputs for payment of duty towards the final product irrespective of when the final product is cleared and whether a particular batch of inputs have gone into that particular batch of the final product. In the Rules, it is seen, so far as an event of taking credit is concerned that is provided for separately under Rule 57A and the event of utilisation of the credit has been provided for separately under Rule 57F and if the credit has been wrongly taken, the same can be reversed or recovered within a period of six months or 5 years as provided for under Rule 57I. The same would apply in case the said credit has been wrongly utilised. But each event will have to be dealt with separately."

3. Respondents cannot be called upon to pay back the credit utilised as pleaded by the revenue. "...............there is no dispute in regard to the taking of the credit and since we have held that the credit has been correctly utilised, the respondents cannot be called upon to pay back the credit utilised as pleaded by the Revenue."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat Credit (Modvat) - OE goods cleared without duty under Chapter X procedure--Whether Modvat admissible--Referred to Larger Bench in view of conflicting decisions

FACT: The appellants receive duly paid bi-metal strips for use in the manufacture of I.C. Engines and parts thereof. They avail of Modvat Credit for the inputs. The appellants cleared certain parts like plain shaft bearings at nil rate of duty by following Chapter X procedure. The Assistant Collector held that credit could not be allowed on inputs used in the manufacture of parts cleared at nil rate of duty as per provisions of Rule 57C of the Central Excise Rules, 1944. This was upheld by the Collector (Appeals).

HELD: Though one to one co-relation of inputs with final product is not prescribed, there appears to be a tacit requirement of reading Rule 57C into the provisions of Rule 57F(3)(i). However in view of the fact that decisions of two Benches run somewhat contrary to each other, the issue "whether credit of duty paid on inputs used in the manufacture of declared final product part of which is cleared without payment of duty could be disallowed" should be placed before a Larger Bench for decision. "Though one to one co-relation is not prescribed under Rule 57F(3)(i), there appears to be a tacit requirement of reading Rule 57C into the provisions of Rule 57F(3)(i). This is the view taken by the East Regional Bench, which we also share to a certain extent. .......Since the issues involves consideration of these points of law and the decisions for two Benches run somewhat contrary to each other, we consider it fit for placing before the larger Bench, for deciding on the following questions.

"Whether, in the context of the provisions of Rule 57C vis-a-vis Rule 57F(3)(i) of the Central Excise Rules, Modvat credit of duty paid on inputs used in the manufacture of declared final products, part of which are cleared free of the whole of duty of excise leviable thereon, in terms of an exemption Notification, could be disallowed by way of reversal of credit of duty on such inputs, which have been used in the manufacture of final products cleared free of duty"?"

HEADNOTE: Section Rule 57A and Section Rule 57G of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat Credit - Graphite rods used for making moulds for manufacturing diamond drilling bits not eligible as moulds are appliances - Limitation-Modvat--SC notice for wrongful availment of Modvat, not hit by time bar

FACT: The appellants are engaged in the manufacture of diamond drilling bits. For this purpose they bring graphite rods from outside on payment of duty and convert them into graphite moulds of different sizes and shapes which are used in the process of sintering in the furnace at high temperature for manufacture of diamond drilling bits. They availed of Modvat credit on graphite rods. The Asstt. Collector held that they were not entitled to Modvat credit on graphite rods as these are used in the manufacture of graphite moulds which, in turn, are used as "appliances", and not in relation to manufacture of diamond drilling bits. The appellants also pleaded that the show cause notice was hit by limitation under section 11A, CESA. On appeal, the Collector (Appeals) upheld the order of the Asstt. Collector. Hence this appeal.

HELD: Modvat--Inputs used "in relation to manufacture"--Graphite rods converted into graphite moulds are used in relation to the manufacture of diamond drilling bits and not directly in the manufacture of diamond drilling bits, as these are not used as raw material or component parts of the finished goods, but the process in which they are used is so integrally connected with the ultimate production of goods that but for it the manufacture or processing of goods would be impossible or commercially inexpedient. "The Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that manufacture involves series of processes. Process in manufacture or in relation to manufacture implies not only the production but the various stages through which the raw material is subjected to change by different operations. It is the cumulative effect of the various processes to which the raw material is subjected to, manufactured product emerges. Therefore, each step towards such production would be a process in relation to the manufacture. Where any particular process is so integrally connected with the ultimate production of goods that but for that process manufacture or processing of goods would be impossible or commercially inexpedient that process is one in relation to the manufacture.......In the case before us graphite rods converted into graphite-moulds are used not as raw material or component part of the finished product--diamond drilling bits. We have, however, taken a view that they are used in relation to the manufacture of the diamond drilling bits."

2. Modvat--Appliances excluded from applicability of Rule 57A CE Rules--Graphite rods converted into graphite moulds are used as "appliances", as these moulds are applied in one heat/sintering process in the furnace to bind particles of powdered metals to form the bits. Hence, graphite rods are excluded from the applicability of Rule 57A and are not eligible for Modvat credit. "The appellants themselves have called the material used in the furnace as graphite-mould. These moulds are used for one heat/sintering process. These moulds as such are not used in the manufacture of diamond drilling bits, for the purposes of Rule 57D of the Rules. These graphite moulds processed from graphite rods are applied in the furnace to bind particles of the powdered metals to form the bits. In this process referred to by the party as sintering process, the graphite rods converted into graphite moulds are used as an 'appliance'. As appliances used for producing or processing of any goods or for bringing about any change in any substance in or in relation to the manufacture of the final products, are excluded from the applicability of Rule 57A, the graphite rods used in relation to the manufacture of diamond drilling bits are not the inputs for the purposes of that Rule........Accordingly, we hold that the credit of the duty of excise paid on graphite-rods is not allowed for utilisation towards payment of duty of excise leviable on the diamond "drilling bits."

3. Limitation--The show cause notice is not time barred as the limitation laid down under section 11A CESA is not applicable to cases of wrongful availment of Modvat credit under Rule 57I. Section 11A occupies the general field while Rule 57I deals with specific field of wrongful availment of Modvat credit [ratio of Gujarat High Court judgment in Torrent Laboratories Ltd. v. UOI, 1991(32) ECR 381 (Gujarat)]. "In the case - Torrent Laboratories Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India.......the Hon'ble Gujarat High Court..........did not accept the contention that the provisions of Section 11A of the Act as regards the period of limitation should be read into Rule 57I.......

, other than machinery, should be complete items functioning independently is only an academic question. There can be some exceptions like certain tools, but these exceptions do not detract form the thrust of the decision. "The question posed whether all the items listed other than machinery in the Explanation Clause should be complete items capable of independent functioning is an academic question. By their very nature, they are such complete items functioning independently. Some exceptions like certain tools and instruments do not detract from the thrust of the decision." 6. Tariff classification of certain items outside Section XVI as machines, appliances or parts thereof, is no impediment to those items being treated as such. However, such is not the case with felt and wire netting. Question raised is of academic nature and one of fact, needing no reference to High Court "This again is an academic question having no practical application in the present case. ............When these articles are referred to as machines or part of machines in the Tariff itself, their Tariff classification outside Section XVI is no impediment to their identity as such machines, appliances or parts of machines. Such is not the case with felts and wire netting. They are neither machines nor parts thereof and they are also not known as such machines/parts. The question posed is one of fact which does not require to be referred to the High Court."

7. Tribunal's order holding felt and wire-netting for paper making machinery, and chemicals used for water treatment, as eligible for modvat benefit was based on several factors and ratio of several judgment of Supreme Court and High Courts. Criteria laid down by Supreme Court in Ballarpur judgment are satisfied, and there is no justification for making reference to the High Court Reference application and stay applications are dismissed/rejected. "The order granting modvat benefit is based on several factors following the ratio of several decisions discussed therein. As far as felt and wire netting are concerned, it has been held that these are neither the excluded items in the Explanation under Rule 57A nor parts of such items. Not being machines, machinery etc. which are the excluded items, they qualify for modvat benefit. .............We have now considered the contentions raised by the Collector citing the Ballarpur judgment of the Supreme Court wherein the criterion of utilisation in the manufacturing process as distinct from the manufacturing apparatus had been laid down. We have found that this criterion is satisfied by the inputs in question which are not used as manufacturing apparatus. We have held them to be outside the zone of exclusion spelt out in Rule 57A...... ........The enlarged scope of "in relation to" would, without any doubt, bring the process of water treatment carried out in relation to the manufacture of paper within the requirements of Rule 57A. The use of the inputs in any anterior process and not directly in the manufacturing process of paper had been adequately covered by the Ballarpur judgment. ......Respectfully following the decisions of the Supreme Court and the various High Courts on the issues involved as well as on the question of reference, we dismiss the present Reference Applications. ....In view of our orders on the Reference Applications, the Stay Petitions preferred by the Collector do not merit consideration and are rejected as such.

8. Observations contained in the Collector's Reference Applications stretched beyond reasonable limits meaning of expression 'inputs' are viewed with total disapproval. "Before parting with the case, we have to express our total disapproval of the observations contained in the Reference Applications about stretching the meaning of the expression 'inputs' to limits beyond reason by incomplete examination of statutory provisions and overlooking/misinterpreting the exclusion provisions. .......While it is entirely open to the Collector to point out errors in the order requiring a Reference, to call into question the order with snide references to stretching the meaning to limits beyond reason by incomplete examination etc. is totally unwarranted. While we would certainly welcome applications to have doubtful questions of law referred to the High Courts for obtaining the benefit of their advice, the scope of such a reference in the present case does not exist, for the reasons exhaustively dealt with by us. For that matter, the order also has followed several decisions discussed elaborately. The effect of these have been totally missed by the Collector and an offensive Reference Application has been made, incidentally, stretching the meaning beyond reason, misinterpreting etc. by itself may not give rise to questions of law requiring reference but only if, by such aberrations or otherwise, doubtful or faulty conclusions are drawn."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit

HELD: Modvat - Denial not sustainable where non-levy was not due to default by input manufacturer and proper records were kept. ".......where the initial non-levy was not due to any default or irregularity on the part of the manufacturer and duty is recovered later on by the department, it will be totally iniquitous to deny the benefit of modvat, particularly where the records maintained are amenable to scrutiny and verification."

HEADNOTE: Section 11A of the Central Excise Act, 1944 read with Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 and Section 35G of the Central Excise Act, 1944 - Demands duties not levied or not paid or short paid - Reference - Modvat--Use of soft paper for manufacture of paper product is not a question of law--Modvat--Limitation applicable under ceased to be a question of law after incorporation of limitation in Central Excise Rule 57-I

FACT: The applicants utilised Modvat credit under Rule 57A CE Rules on kraft paper used for packing the final product Linoleums. The Department held that under Notification No. 177/86-CE dt. 1.3.1986 credit in respect of paper used "in the manufacture of final product" was to be restricted to Rs. 800/- per tonne. The applicants' case is that they used the kraft paper "in relation to the manufacture of the final product", as "packing material" is recognised as an input under Explanation to Rule 57A. The Tribunal upheld the Department's view but found the Notice time-barred. In this Reference Application, the main question raised by applicants for reference is whether the expression "in relation to the manufacture" used in Rule 57A is synonymous to the expression "in the manufacture" used in the abovesaid notification. By the Cross Objection, the Department wants reference of the question whether the time limit prescribed in amended Rule 57-I is applicable in respect of an offence committed earlier to the amendment.

HELD: Reference--Question of law--The question whether the expression "in or in relation to the manufacture of final products" used in Rule 57A, and the expression "in the manufacture of final products" used in Notification No. 177/86-CE are synonymous does not arise from the Tribunal's order which examined the statutory definition of "manufacture" and concluded that kraft paper has been used in this case "in the manufacture" of the final product, as wrapping paper. (Ratio of Supreme Court's judgment in CCE v. East End Paper Industries Ltd. and in J.K. Cotton Spg. Wvg. Mills Co. Ltd. v. S.T.O.). "In view of the categoric finding in the order in question that Kraft Paper has been used in the manufacture of final product, linoleum, rejecting the contention to the contrary that it is not so used but only in relation to the manufacture of such final product, the questions of law suggested for reference lose their significance. Thus, for example, Question A in the application is as to whether the two expressions "goods used in or in relation to the manufacture of the final products" appearing in Rule 57A and the expression "goods used in the manufacture of final products" appearing in the 3rd proviso to Notification 177/86 dated 1.3.1986 are synonymous is an academic question with the answer self-evident. It does not arise from the Tribunal's order which also did not proceed on the basis that the two expressions were synonymous. The order also did not seek to apply the restriction in the quantum of modvat benefit applicable under the Notification in question to inputs used only in relation to the manufacture by equating both the expressions. It was, on the contrary, held on the strength of the statutory definition of the expression "manufacture" that the use was only in the manufacture and their contention was rejected on this score only".

. Inputs used for generation of electricity would qualify for MODVAT credit only if they are used in or in relation to the manufacture of the final product, such as cement, caustic soda, etc. Therefore, it is not correct to state that inputs used as fuel for generation of electricity captively consumed will not be covered as inputs under rule 57A. [Para 8] However, in some of the cases, electricity generated was consumed by the residential colony of the factory’s workers’ families, schools, etc., to that extent MODVAT credit would not be admissible. [Para 9]

Therefore, there was no merit in the civil appeal filed by the department and accordingly it was to be dismissed. [Para 10]

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat Credit - Modvat - Wire mesh and woollen felts used in paper making machines are not inputs; hence Modvat benefit not permissible

FACT: The appellants claimed Modvat credit for wire mesh and woollen felts which was denied on the ground that the items are in the nature of appliances.

HELD: Modvat--Inputs--Wire mesh and woollen felts are used to make the paper making machine functional, and not directly for manufacture of paper. Therefore, the benefit of Modvat credit is not permissible (ratio of Tribunal Order No. 299/90 SRB dated 4.4.1990). "We observe that the two items are used in the paper machine section of the paper mill and the use of these two items in the paper machines is to make the machine functional. This Bench of the Tribunal, as pointed out by the Ld. Consultant at the very outset, has given detailed reasons as to why these items have to be precluded from the benefit of Modvat credit."

rule 57G and rule 57T. [Para 9]

Applying the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in various cases to the facts of the instant case, it was to be held that the amendment made in rule 57G of the Rules by insertion of sub-rule (11) vide Notification No. 7/99, dated 9-2-1999 relates to procedure for availing Modvat credit and does not effect any substantive right. [Para 35] From the conjoint reading of rules 52A, 57G and the amendment made by Notification No. 7/99, dated 9-2-1999 by which sub-rule (11) was inserted in rule 57G, of filing of the documents for availing Modvat credit is only a procedural matter and the amendment made vide Notification No. 7/99, dated 9-2-1999 which inserted sub-rule (11) in rule 57G the position was made clear that Modvat credit should not be denied only on the ground that the documents referred to in sub-rule (2) does not strictly comply with the said rule but contains the details of payment dues, description of goods, assessable value, name and address of the factory or warehouse etc. This position has also been clarified by the Central Board of Excise and Customs by issuing a circular in exercise of its power under section 37B of the Act and made it applicable to all pending cases. [Para 36]

The submission of the revenue that the Notification No. 7/99, dated 9-2-1999 would come into effect on the date of its publication i.e., 9-2-1999 only, may be correct but the benefit of that Notification as directed by the Central Board of Excise and Customs has been extended to all the pending cases. The provision of sub-rule (2) is procedural for availing Modvat credit, the benefit of sub-rule (11) is available to the assessee. [Para 39]

HEADNOTE: Rule 57 of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Cenvat Credit (Modvat) - Modvat - Limitation - Runs Relevant from the date of credit and not of utilisation for payment of duty or submission of RT-12 return

HELD: Modvat - limitation--The relevant date for computation of limitation under Rule 57I(1) is the date of credit and not the one of its utilisation for payment of duty or date of submission of RT-12 return which will be subsequent to the date of credit The contention of the Department that the limitation period of six months is to be computed from the date of submission of monthly RT-12 returns filed .....and not from the date of taking credit, is without force, in view of the finality of the matter as expressed by the Tribunal in the case of Arunachal Plywood Industries v. CCE ... and CCE, Patna v. Asia Insulated Wires (P) Ltd. .....--it has been held therein that the relevant date for computation of limitation under amended Rule 57-I(1)(1) the date of credit and not the one of its utilisation for payment of duty or date of submission of RT-12 return which will be subsequent to the date of credit."

HEADNOTE: Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules, 1944 - Modvat credit - Input - Lancing pipe used for passing oxygen into furnace for melting of metal, comes into contact of molten steel and is wholly consumed in process - Tribunal held that these were eligible for Modvat credit - Whether no question of law arose out of order of Tribunal - Held, yes

FACT: The Tribunal held that the product ‘lancing pipe’ used for passing oxygen gas into molten metal for rapid melting of scrap into liquid steel was to be considered as input and was eligible for Modvat credit.

On application :

HELD: The Tribunal had observed that the lancing pipes are used for discharge of oxygen into the furnace to cut open the top holes provided in the furnace to draw out metals from furnace. Lancing pipe while cutting open the holes, comes into contact with the molten steel in the furnace. On account of the high temperature in the furnace, these pipes melt and join the steel. While so the lancing pipe gets wholly consumed in the process. The pipe so consumed form part of the molten metal which is being taken out of the furnace. Since this pipe gets so consumed in the process, it was entitled to Modvat credit. [Para 3]

In view of the aforesaid facts, no substantial question of law arose in the instant application. The application was to be dismissed. [Para 7]

(xi)

PVC Pipes

The Tribunal allowed credit on aforesaid 11 items.

The department argued that the assessee is not entitled for such credit as the inputs are not used directly or indirectly for the manufacture of final products and they are not eligible for credit under rule 57A.

The assessee argued that the precedent judgments had allowed credit.

Issue Involved

Whether aforesaid 11 items were eligible for credit ?

HELD: The item-wise treatment is as follows : Rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules deals with credit of duty paid on the excisable goods used as inputs. Rule 57Q relates to credit of duty paid on capital goods used by the manufacturer of specified goods. The Tribunal had relied on assessee's own case in Madras Aluminium Co. Ltd. v. CCE 2001 (136) (ELT) 182 (Tri-Chennai). The said order deals only with 57A of the Central Excise Rules, where many of the inputs were considered for credit. Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in holding that the inputs are used directly or indirectly for the manufacture of final product as per rule 57A of the Central Excise Rules during the relevant period. [Para 18]

Therefore, the assessee is entitled for credit for the above said items. [Para 19]
